newsitem.title: USA: Senior Democrat wants probe of party fundraising.
newsitem.headline: Senior Democrat wants probe of party fundraising.

text.p: Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan has become the first Democrat to call for an independent counsel to probe his party's fundraising during last year's election campaign, the New York Post reported Thursday.

In a meeting with the newspaper's editors and reporters, the New York Democrat said there should be a probe of both parties' fundraising, adding that it was the possibility of foreign involvement he was most concerned about.
The paper quoted Moynihan as saying he thought it was ridiculous to claim "everyone has Chinese arms merchants to lunch -- don't you?"
He was referring to President Clinton's having met Wang Jun, the head of a weapons trading firm owned by the Chinese government, at a White House coffee meeting in February, 1996.
Attorney General Janet Reno has so far refused Republican calls for an independent counsel and the Post said Moynihan was the first Democrat to make an outright call for one.
The independent counsel statute was created after the Watergate scandal to ensure unbiased investigations of potential wrongdoing by officials of the executive branch.

Moynihan said naming such a counsel "would be damaging" to Vice President Al Gore because of Gore's involvement in a fund-raiser during last year's presidential campaign at a Buddhist temple in which several donations had to be returned for breaking fund-raising rules.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry declined all comment on Moynihan's remarks.
